newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Pepsi's bottler says it lost $152 million in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Pepsi's bottler says it lost $152 million in quarter.

text.p: Argentina's Buenos Aires Embotelladora SA, the biggest Pepsi Co. bottler outside the United States, said Tuesday it lost nearly $152 million in the latest quarter.
BAESA told the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange that it lost $151.6 million in its fiscal fourth quarter ended on Sept. 30, compared with a profit of $5.4 million a year ago.
On Monday, BAESA said it lost $426.4 million in the year to Sept. 30. The results include an extraordinary loss of $126.3 million, BAESA said.
In July, Pepsi took over control of BAESA, which has suffered a financial crunch that many analysts blame on overexpansion.

BAESA has the exclusive Pepsi and Seven-Up franchises for the Buenos Aires metropolitan area and other regions in Argentina, as well as Chile, Uruguay and Costa Rica and some Southern Brazilian states, including the metropolitan areas of Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.

The company said fourth quarter sales in Argentina fell 8 percent to $70.2 million and the company had an operating loss of $23.8 million, excluding the impact of accounting adjustments and restructuring costs.
In Brazil, its revenues sank 31 percent to $53.6 million and it reported an operating loss of $48.1 million.
BAESA's stockholders in September filed a class action suit in federal court in New York City against both BAESA and Pepsi alleging they hid the bottler's problems.
In October BAESA announced a standstill agreement with its leading creditors to defer until March 31 repayments of $520 million in debts.
